pages.title: Declaring and Initializing Arrays in JavaScript
pages.content:
# Introduction to JavaScript Arrays

An array is an ordered collection of values. In JavaScript, arrays are resizable and can hold elements of mixed data types.

### Creating Arrays
- **Array literal notation (Recommended)**: `const list = [1, 2, 3];`
- **Array constructor**: `const list = new Array(1, 2, 3);`

### Indexing and Length
JavaScript arrays are zero-indexed. The `.length` property reflects the number of elements in the array.

```javascript
const fruits = ["Apple", "Banana", "Cherry"];
console.log(fruits[0]); // "Apple"
console.log(fruits.length); // 3
console.log(fruits[fruits.length - 1]); // Last item: "Cherry"
```

Modern JavaScript also provides `fruits.at(-1)` to access elements from the end using negative indexes.

callout.title: at() Method
callout.text: The Array.prototype.at(index) method accepts negative integers to count back from the last item: list.at(-1) returns the last item.

checkpoint.question: Which method or syntax retrieves the last element of an array using negative indexing in modern JavaScript?
checkpoint.explanation: arr.at(-1) accepts negative integers to index from the end of the array.

pages.title: Array Mutator Methods (push, pop, shift, unshift)
pages.content:
# Adding and Removing Array Elements

JavaScript arrays provide convenient stack and queue methods that mutate the array in-place:

### End Operations (Stack)
- **`push(...items)`**: Appends one or more elements to the **end** of the array. Returns the new length.
- **`pop()`**: Removes and returns the **last** element of the array.

### Beginning Operations (Queue)
- **`unshift(...items)`**: Inserts one or more elements at the **beginning**. Returns the new length.
- **`shift()`**: Removes and returns the **first** element of the array.

```javascript
const queue = [2, 3];
queue.push(4);    // [2, 3, 4]
queue.unshift(1); // [1, 2, 3, 4]
queue.pop();      // removes 4 -> [1, 2, 3]
queue.shift();    // removes 1 -> [2, 3]
```

callout.title: Performance Note
callout.text: push() and pop() operate in O(1) amortized time, while shift() and unshift() require re-indexing all existing elements, taking O(N) time.

checkpoint.question: Which array method removes the first element from an array and returns it?
checkpoint.explanation: shift() removes the first element from an array and returns that removed element.

pages.title: Slicing, Splicing, and Concatenating Arrays
pages.content:
# Slicing, Splicing, and Joining Arrays

Distinguishing between mutating and non-mutating operations is essential in JavaScript:

### `slice(start, end)` (Non-Mutating)
Returns a shallow copy of a portion of an array into a new array. The original array is unchanged.
```javascript
const nums = [10, 20, 30, 40];
const sub = nums.slice(1, 3); // [20, 30]
```

### `splice(start, deleteCount, ...items)` (Mutating)
Changes the contents of an array in-place by removing or replacing existing elements and/or adding new elements.
```javascript
const months = ['Jan', 'March', 'April'];
months.splice(1, 0, 'Feb'); // Inserts 'Feb' at index 1
console.log(months); // ['Jan', 'Feb', 'March', 'April']
```

### `concat(...arrays)` (Non-Mutating)
Merges two or more arrays and returns a new combined array.

callout.title: slice vs splice
callout.text: Remember: slice returns a slice of the array without modifying it. splice alters (splices) the original array directly.

checkpoint.question: What is the key difference between array.slice() and array.splice()?
options: slice() modifies the original array, while splice() does not
splice() modifies the original array in-place, while slice() returns a new array
slice() only works on numbers, while splice() works on strings
checkpoint.explanation: splice() alters the contents of an array in-place, whereas slice() returns a shallow copy of a portion into a new array.

practiceProblems.title: Creating Arrays
practiceProblems.description:
**Arrays** are a fundamental data structure in JavaScript that allows you to store and organize collections of data. Whether you're dealing with a list of numbers, strings, or more complex objects, arrays provide a convenient way to manage and manipulate your data.

`Arrays`  are used to store multiple values in a single variable, instead of declaring separate variables for each value.

In JS, an array is denoted by square brackets **[ ]** 
- It can hold elements of different data types, such as numbers, strings,  or even other lists. 
- Arrays are mutable, which means you can modify them by adding, removing, or changing elements.

Consider the array  `'fruits'`  and  `'numbers'`  below
```javascript
var fruits = ["apple", "banana", "orange", "grape"];

var numbers = [20, 10, 0, -5];
```

### Task
Write a program which does the following
- Create an  `Array`  of the first 5 positive integers - name it  **`integers`**
- Once the array is defined - output  **"Done"**  to the console.

practiceProblems.title: Changing the elements of an Array
practiceProblems.description:
You can also modify elements in an array by assigning a new value to a specific index.
```javascript
var fruits = ["apple", "banana", "orange", "grape"]
fruits[1] = "kiwi"
console.log(fruits);  // Output: ["apple", "kiwi", "orange", "grape"]
```

### Task
Write a program which does the following.
- The 3rd month in the given array is incorrect.
- Update the 3rd month in the given  `array`  with the correct one -  `"Mar"`.
- Once the 3rd  `array`  element is updated, output the entire array to the console.

practiceProblems.title: Slicing a list
practiceProblems.description:
Similar to what we saw in slicing of  `strings`,  you can slice arrays as well. \
You can specify a range of consecutive indexes by specifying where to start and where to end the range in this manner -  `console.log(arr.slice(1, 4));`.\
This will print elements from  `index number`  **`1`**  to **`3`**.

**Note**:
- Indexing starts from 0.
- Item on index no  **`4`**  will not be printed as the end index is excluded.

For eg - 
```javascript
arr = ["Juke", "King", "Hearts", "68", "Kite"];
console.log(arr.slice(1, 4));
```
The output will be
```javascript
["King", "Hearts", "68"]
```

Write a program which does the following:
- Create a list  **`months`**  of the first 7 months in a year.
- Output the following to the console on separate lines:
   - Print the list containing first  **`6`**  months of the year.
   - Print the list containing 2nd to 5th month of the year - both 2nd and 5th included.

questions.question: Which method appends one or more elements to the end of an array and returns the new length?
questions.explanation: push() appends items to the end of an array and returns the array's updated length.

questions.question: How do you check if an object is a genuine JavaScript Array?
questions.explanation: Array.isArray(obj) is the standard and most reliable method to determine whether a value is an Array.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].pop() return?
questions.explanation: pop() removes the last element of an array and returns that removed element (3).

questions.question: What does [10, 20, 30].indexOf(50) return?
questions.explanation: indexOf() returns -1 if the search element is not found.

questions.question: What does ['a', 'b', 'c'].join('-') return?
questions.explanation: join('-') concatenates all elements of an array into a single string separated by the specified delimiter ('a-b-c').

questions.question: Which method removes elements from an array and optionally inserts new elements in their place in-place?
questions.explanation: splice() changes the contents of an array by removing, replacing, or adding elements in-place.

questions.question: What is the result of [1, 2, 3].includes(2)?
questions.explanation: includes() returns true if the value is present in the array.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3].reverse() do to the original array?
options: Returns a new reversed array leaving the original unchanged
Reverses the array in-place and mutates the original
Throws a TypeError unless sorted first
Only reverses if numbers are consecutive
questions.explanation: Array.prototype.reverse() reverses an array in-place and mutates the original array.

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3, 4, 5].slice(1, 4) return?
questions.explanation: slice(1, 4) starts at index 1 and ends before index 4, returning [2, 3, 4].

questions.question: Can an array in JavaScript contain elements of differing data types simultaneously?
options: No, all elements must share the exact same type
Yes, arrays can hold mixed primitives, objects, and nested arrays
Only if initialized with the Array constructor
questions.explanation: JavaScript arrays are dynamically typed and can hold any combination of numbers, strings, booleans, objects, and functions.
